svg.title: AgentDojo execution components and loop
svg.desc: The task and environment enter AgentPipeline. The adapter sends history to the model interface; parsed responses flow through the tool executor and runtime. Tool results return to history for the next request. The native evaluator evaluates the returned pipeline. A passive observer records events, and HTML is generated after the run. The selected timeline event determines the highlight.

g.text: Tool messages enter history and the next request
No final text: up to 3 attempts

g.title: The runner manages benchmark execution, native logs, and result summaries. RUN_END status is not task utility.
AgentDojo supplies the user task, initial environment, tool set, and evaluation rules. This initialization has no dedicated runtime event.
Each complete query is an episode. EPISODE_STARTED occurs before system-prompt and user-query initialization.
Stores system, user, assistant, and tool messages. Tool results in history may be included in multiple requests.
The Groq adapter converts native messages and tool definitions. The observer records the actual JSON body at the outbound HTTP boundary.
FunctionsRuntime validates arguments, fills defaults, and injects dependencies before calling local tools. Entry arguments and raw returns have separate events.
ToolsExecutionLoop checks whether to continue. ToolsExecutor validates tool names, adjusts argument formatting, and executes batches. There is no separate executor-entry event.
Converts the HTTP response into a native assistant message and records proposed tool calls. These proposals have not executed yet.
Only request and response boundaries are recorded. The model's internal reasoning and actual attention cannot be determined here.
Simulates email, calendars, cloud storage, and other environments. ENVIRONMENT_CHANGE indicates a state change across a tool call; environment snapshots are not model input.
After a batch completes, the executor formats returns or errors as tool messages and adds them to history. Unknown tools may produce error messages without entering the runtime.
A pipeline return or error does not establish task completion; calls may still be pending. The suite reruns the pipeline if needed, up to three attempts in total.
The native evaluator assesses utility after the pipeline and any required retries. There is no dedicated evaluator event; this node provides architectural context.
ObservationSession and EventRecorder passively record events at these boundaries without modifying or intercepting agent actions.
g.text: Observes execution boundaries; does not decide actions

g.title: After the run, reads the summary, native conversations, and events to generate HTML that opens offline. This process has no dedicated runtime event.
g.text: After the run → local HTML report
